patient.chief_complaint: Husband called 911 - wife has faciobrachial dystonic seizures now continuous 15 minutes, status epilepticus
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Hughes is a 47-year-old woman with known anti-LGI1 autoimmune encephalitis treated 8 months ago who presents with continuous faciobrachial dystonic seizures (FBDS) that have been occurring every 1-2 minutes for the past 15 minutes without return to baseline. Anti-LGI1 encephalitis is characterized by pathognomonic faciobrachial dystonic seizures — brief unilateral facial twitching with ipsilateral arm dystonic posturing, typically lasting <3 seconds and occurring very frequently (up to 100/day at worst). She had been doing well on levetiracetam, mycophenolate, and tapering prednisone. Over the past 2 weeks her husband noticed she was having more frequent FBDS and seemed confused at times. She had her LGI1 antibody titer checked last month which was positive (1:32, down from 1:128 at diagnosis). Her neurologist recently tapered prednisone from 10 mg to 5 mg daily. The prednisone taper may have triggered a disease relapse. She is now in FBDS status epilepticus — a recognized form of SE in anti-LGI1 encephalitis. Importantly, traditional AEDs are often relatively ineffective for FBDS — immunotherapy is the primary treatment. Her mycophenolate may need dose escalation or IVIG/steroids reinstitution. LGI1 antibody titer recheck is essential.
